rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call is the slide changed today, chunk 8 "Pre-reads before Module 3": line 79: "Module 3 draws that boundary for your own repo." — "that boundary" resolves inside the same sentence pair on the same slide ("what it can reach, what it must not touch, and where the blast radius ends"), so it needs no prior-slide history at all. Second closest, chunk 8: line 81: "and the rest of the surface" — "the surface" was named two paragraphs up on the SAME slide (line 77: "into a compromise surface"), in-chunk. Third, chunk 5: line 46: "a branch from the second-pass read" — sequential-read resolution comes from the module include order carve-out (rule 1, module-arc beats): chunk 4 inlines `exercises/push-back-on-the-plan.md`, whose body names the second-pass read at its lines 5, 62, 68, 111 (verified by grep, output pasted in rule 3's evidence). Variant B chunk 8b line 83: "The thinking Module 4 asks you to do" — self-carrying. No pronoun in the body is left without an in-chunk or earlier-chunk antecedent.

Closest call, chunk 2 "Prework": line 14: "And if Dex Horthy's [Why Software Factories Fail](...) is still on your list from Module 1" — names the source by TITLE plus its claim unpacked in the same sentence ("the cure he lands on is human review made affordable by upfront planning"), which is the passing shape §2 prints. "from Module 1" locates a module by name, not a slide by position. Chunk 8's "Module 3 draws that boundary" and chunk 8b's "Module 4 asks you to do" are forward navigational pointers, NAMED not located — §2's navigational carve-out. Zero instances of the banned shape ("the opening lecture said", "the earlier slide") in the body: `sed -n '1,94p' <file> | grep -nEi 'the (opening|previous|last|earlier) (lecture|slide|exercise)'` → 0 matches.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two backward references in the body, both resolved against the module's CURRENT include set (chunk 4 lines 28-34: the-whole-map, when-a-plan-is-good, push-back-on-the-plan, extract-the-task-shaping-rule; chunk 5 lines 64-66: where-the-rule-could-live, how-instructions-grow). (a) chunk 5 line 46: "a branch from the second-pass read" — RAN `grep -rn "second-pass\|second read\|walk down\|walk-down" curriculum/exercises/push-back-on-the-plan.md ...` → real output includes `push-back-on-the-plan.md:5: **What you do:** push back twice on your plan, run a second-pass grilling` and `:68: The second read runs in this same session and still in plan mode`. Beat exists. (b) chunk 9 line 89: "you point the same move at a feature you're shipping" — "the same move" is this module's own plan-read move, named across chunks 3, 4 and 5. No dead beat.

rules_evaluated.evidence: N/A — no guess-before-reveal beat anywhere in the body. `sed -n '1,94p' <file> | grep -nEi 'take a guess|guess before|predict|before you (watch|run|see)'` → 0 matches; the module file carries no demo narration at all (demos live in the inlined lecture/exercise files, which are judged separately).

Smallest chunk is 1 "Big Idea" at 19 words (from check-slide-size.js --report, pasted under rule 14) and it carries a complete standalone claim: line 6: "The first plan is plausible. Plausible isn't good enough, and you are the one who can tell the difference." Next smallest, chunk 9 "Next" at 46 words, likewise self-carrying. No chunk is a wait-state or a single context-dependent bullet. Note: the two Start-here connectives that WERE orphans were already cut — maintainer block line 111 records it.

Closest call is the changed chunk 8: header "Pre-reads before Module 3" over content that is now three entries, two labelled **Read:** and one **Optional deeper scan:**. The header still reads true — an optional deeper scan is a pre-read offered before Module 3, and line 75 ("Optional.") states the whole block's status up front, so the header does not over-promise required reading. Every other header is literally true of its chunk ("Save the rule if it earned itself" over a conditional-compound ritual that explicitly permits stopping, line 46).

All six sub-items checked per chunk. (a) "Not X. Not Y. Z.": RAN `sed -n '1,94p' <file> | grep -c 'Not [A-Za-z]*\. Not '` → 0. (b) anaphora/epistrophe triples: closest is the changed chunk 8, line 79: "what it can reach, what it must not touch, and where the blast radius ends" — a three-item list where the third leg carries genuinely new content (blast radius, not access), and its variant-B twin at line 83 swaps the third leg for "how you will know afterwards whether it went well". Both pass the new-content test; neither is a sentence-initial anaphora triple. (c) self-grading superlatives (the blocking sub-item, value-prop leak): RAN `sed -n '1,94p' <file> | grep -nEi 'one of the most|most useful|the single best|game.chang' | wc -l` → 0. (d) number + own retraction: chunk 6 line 69: "Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part" — no retraction clause attached, and maintainer block line 119 attests the shape explicitly ("§7's number-plus-retraction sub-item does not fire here (no retraction attached)"). (e) abstraction-noun stacks: chunk 6 line 71: "Assumption-silent isn't assumption-free" is a coined pair immediately cashed out in the same bullet ("every plan assumes something, the good ones say what"). (f) empty verb legs: no verb triplet in the body.

rules_evaluated.evidence: RAN `sed -n '1,94p' <file> | grep -nEo 'compendium|forcing function|firing|Connections' | sort | uniq -c` → zero output (empty). Closest judgement call is the changed chunk 8: line 77: "into a compromise surface" and line 81: "the rest of the surface" — surface-as-noun, which §8 names as dialect. It stays inside: "attack/compromise surface" is standard security vocabulary for AE101's engineer ICs, not repo-authorial vocabulary, and §8's own audience-register clause says to weigh register before firing. The phrase is also the Willison piece's own framing being reported, not our house term. "Big Idea" and "Key Concepts" headers are architecture-mandated section names, explicitly NOT dialect per §8.

Three bolded elements, but this is exactly §9's reading-list/menu waiver (Antti-directed 2026-08-13): the per-slide budget is off, the ≲5-word handle cap still binds, and each handle is the MODE WORD ALONE (1 and 3 words) with every title left plain — the compliant shape, not the mode-plus-title monoculture the waiver warns about. Adding the third entry therefore adds no §9 exposure. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked against the renderer, not long-read, because the changed section is TRAILING module-level prose (it sits after the last `.phase--*` include, chunk 5's lectures at lines 64-66) and that is precisely the shape §10 says can vanish. Read `site/layouts/slides.js` `buildDeckModel` lines 274-300: module-level children are pushed to `buf`, `flushProse()` fires on each `.phase--*`, and — load-bearing here — there is a final bare `flushProse();` at line 300 AFTER the `forEach` closes. So `## Pre-reads before Module 3`, `## Pre-reads before Module 4` and `## Next` all reach the composed deck as slides under the M2 section code. Corroborated independently by check-slide-size.js, which resolves through the renderer's own `applyContentFlags` and reports 9 slides for this file including "Pre-reads before Module 3" — a section absent from the deck would not be measured.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: RAN `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/plan-mode-done-right.md --report`. Real output, largest first: 169w/0b "Save the rule if it earned itself"; 167w/6b "Key Concepts"; 139w/0b "Prework"; 105w/4b "Optional challenges"; 103w/0b "Pre-reads before Module 3"; 85w/5b "What You'll Learn"; 53w/0b "Start here"; 46w/0b "Next"; 19w/0b "Big Idea". Footer: "files: 1 slides: 9 limits: 210 words / 6 bullets / oversized: 0 / ✓ every slide is within limits". The slide changed today sits at 103 words against a 210 cap — 107 words of headroom, roughly half the ceiling, and 0 bullets against a 6 cap. The `getting-going.md` oversized-reading-list precedent is therefore NOT needed and I did not invoke it: nothing here is over. The M4 variant branch (chunk 8b) is the alternative fork the checker resolves away per §14's runtime-fork clause; counted by hand it is ~85 words, also far under, so neither build oversizes. Bullet-count corpus calibration also holds: Key Concepts at exactly 6, not the 7-outlier §14 warns about.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a module file, so its headings are architecture-mandated section labels (`## Big Idea`, `## Prework`, `## What You'll Learn`, `## Key Concepts`, `## Next`) plus three authored labels. §15 names phase/section labels and orientation headers as NOT violations. Closest call is chunk 5's "Save the rule if it earned itself" — an imperative with a condition attached, which is the exercise-register shape and correct for a section that instructs. The changed header "Pre-reads before Module 3" is a catalogue/orientation label naming its subject — §15's explicit non-violation class, and Antti 2026-08-15: "not every header owes a claim." No declarative-claim beat is being wasted here; the module's one law lands in `## Big Idea`, which the renderer projects as the divider subtitle.
